questions.stem: The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) recently raised the repo rate and shifted its policy stance. With reference to the MPC, consider the following statements: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Monetary Policy Committee of the RBI comprises six members, with the RBI Governor serving as its Chairperson.
Of the six MPC members, three are external members appointed by the Central Government.
The repo rate decided by the MPC is the rate at which the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks against government securities.
Decisions of the MPC require the unanimous consent of all six members before they can be implemented.
questions.explanation: Statements 1-3 are correct statutory and functional facts about the MPC under Section 45ZB of the RBI Act. Statement 4 is wrong: MPC decisions are taken by majority vote, with the Governor holding a casting vote in case of a tie, not by unanimity — even though the October hike happened to be unanimous.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: RBI MPC minutes reveal two members opposed the shift from neutral stance to calibrated tightening in October's meeting
questions.pyqLink: Tests MPC composition and voting rules under RBI Act Sections 45ZB/45ZI; similar to UPSC 2021 Prelims question on the Monetary Policy Committee of the RBI.

questions.stem: News reports note that India's surging solar capacity is straining the grid, forcing 'curtailment' of solar farms. With reference to electricity grid management in India, consider the following statements: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Curtailment refers to the deliberate reduction of power generation from a renewable energy plant below its available potential, usually due to grid or transmission constraints.
Under the Indian Electricity Grid Code, grid frequency must be maintained within a wide band of 48-52 Hz at all times.
Under the Renewable Purchase Obligation framework, electricity distribution licensees are required to source a minimum proportion of their power from renewable energy sources.
Solar power is classified as a 'dispatchable' source of electricity since its output can be precisely scheduled to match demand at any given time.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 correctly describe curtailment and the Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) mechanism under the Electricity Act, 2003. Statement 2 is wrong — the IEGC mandates a much narrower frequency band (close to 49.90-50.05 Hz), not 48-52 Hz. Statement 4 is wrong — solar is a non-dispatchable, intermittent source precisely because its output varies with sunlight, which is the grid-balancing problem the article describes.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Is India's solar power play facing its Icarus moment?
questions.pyqLink: Tests grid code frequency bands and RPO under the Electricity Act, 2003; similar in spirit to UPSC questions on renewable energy integration and the National Electricity Policy.

questions.stem: With reference to Foreign Portfolio Investment (FPI), amid reports of large FPI outflows from Indian equities, consider the following statements: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Foreign Portfolio Investment involves investment in financial assets like shares and bonds and generally carries a shorter investment horizon than Foreign Direct Investment.
Under the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999, FPI transactions are classified as current account transactions.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — FPI (portfolio, liquid, shorter-horizon) is the standard contrast to FDI (controlling stake, longer-horizon). Statement 2 is wrong — under FEMA, 1999, investment in shares/bonds including FPI is a capital account transaction, not a current account one.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: FM Sitharaman flags global capital moving towards US, AI-linked markets as a ‘concern’ for India in 2027
questions.pyqLink: Tests the FDI vs FPI distinction and capital vs current account classification under FEMA, 1999; a recurring UPSC Economy theme (e.g., UPSC 2017 prelims on FDI/FPI).

questions.stem: With reference to the Index of Eight Core Industries (ICI), whose September growth figures were released by the Commerce and Industry Ministry, consider the following statements: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The ICI measures the combined output of eight industries: Coal, Crude Oil, Natural Gas, Refinery Products, Fertilisers, Steel, Cement and Electricity.
The eight core industries together account for a weight of about 40% in the Index of Industrial Production (IIP).
The Index of Eight Core Industries is compiled and released by the Reserve Bank of India on a quarterly basis.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — the ICI's eight constituents and their roughly 40% weight in the IIP are well-established facts. Statement 3 is wrong: the ICI is released monthly by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (as the article itself notes), not quarterly by the RBI, which is a classic near-miss distractor confusing institutional responsibility.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Core sector growth accelerates to 7.9% in September, fastest in new series
questions.pyqLink: Tests composition and publishing authority of the Index of Eight Core Industries and its IIP weight; a recurring Economy-indicators theme in UPSC prelims.

questions.stem: India's semiconductor ecosystem is expanding with fabrication and packaging facilities across several states. With reference to terms used in semiconductor manufacturing, consider the following pairs: How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
pairs: Fabrication (Fab)
Facility where raw silicon wafers are processed into chips through photolithography and doping
OSAT (Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test)
Facility that packages and tests finished chips after fabrication
DRAM
A type of non-volatile memory that retains stored data even without a power supply
Wafer
A thin slice of semiconductor material, typically silicon, used as the base substrate for microelectronic devices
questions.explanation: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 correctly describe fabrication, OSAT, and wafers — the stages referenced in the Dholera fab and Sanand OSAT projects mentioned in the article. Pair 3 is wrong: DRAM (Dynamic Random-Access Memory) is volatile memory — it loses its stored data as soon as power is removed, the opposite of what is stated.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Amitabh Kant on how India's semiconductor future is taking shape: 6 states with 12 projects
questions.pyqLink: Tests basic semiconductor value-chain terminology (fab, OSAT, volatile vs non-volatile memory), an emerging S&T prelims area given India's semiconductor mission.

questions.stem: The India-New Zealand FTA coming into force is noted to give India trade agreements with all RCEP members except China. With reference to the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), which one of the following best describes India's current relationship with this trade bloc?
options: India is a founding member of RCEP and has ratified the agreement along with the other member states.
India took part in RCEP negotiations but withdrew before the agreement was concluded, and is currently not a member of the bloc.
India holds observer status in RCEP and is negotiating entry through a separate bilateral protocol.
India is a member of RCEP but has secured a permanent exemption from all tariff-reduction commitments under the agreement.
questions.explanation: India participated in RCEP negotiations for years but opted out in November 2019 over concerns including the trade deficit with China and impact on domestic agriculture and dairy; the agreement was signed by the remaining 15 members in November 2020 without India, which is why India now lacks an FTA with RCEP's largest economy, China. India holds no observer status or special membership in RCEP.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: India-New Zealand trade pact takes effect on October 20: How it benefits both sides | Key highlights
questions.pyqLink: Tests India's 2019 withdrawal from RCEP and its trade-bloc implications; similar to UPSC 2020 prelims coverage of RCEP.

questions.stem: With reference to the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the RBI, consider the following two statements:
statements: Statement-I: The Monetary Policy Committee's decisions on the policy repo rate are binding on the Reserve Bank of India.
Statement-II: The Monetary Policy Committee is a statutory body constituted under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, as amended in 2016.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. Section 45ZI of the RBI Act makes MPC decisions binding on the Bank, and this binding legal force flows precisely from the MPC's statutory status, created by the 2016 amendment to the RBI Act, 1934 — so Statement-II correctly explains Statement-I. This distinguishes the MPC (a statutory body) from constitutional bodies like the Election Commission.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: RBI MPC Minutes: Governor Sanjay Malhotra ties future hikes to growth-inflation outlook — here is what he said
questions.pyqLink: Tests the statutory (not constitutional) status of the MPC and the legal basis for binding monetary policy decisions; relevant to UPSC's recurring statutory-vs-constitutional-body questions.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding agrivoltaics, as discussed by the MNRE Secretary in the context of India's renewable energy push. How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Agrivoltaics involves simultaneous use of the same land parcel for agricultural cultivation and solar photovoltaic power generation.
The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy is the nodal central ministry for promoting agrivoltaics in India.
Feed-in tariffs for power generated under agrivoltaic projects are notified by the Union Ministry of Power.
Agrivoltaic systems have been found to have no effect on crop yield under any climatic condition.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct by definition of agrivoltaics (land retains its primary agricultural purpose alongside solar generation). Statement 2 is correct — MNRE is the nodal ministry, as confirmed by its Secretary's briefing. Statement 3 is wrong: feed-in tariffs are notified by state governments, not the Union Ministry of Power — state-level enthusiasm and notification speed is what the MNRE Secretary said would determine capacity growth. Statement 4 is wrong: it is an overgeneralised, absolute claim with no basis in the article or in agronomic evidence, where shading effects on yield vary by crop and climate.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: India's agrivoltaic capacity is expected to be more than 5-gigawatts in next 3-4 years: MNRE Secretary
questions.pyqLink: Tests static concept of co-location of agriculture and solar PV and the Centre-State division of renewable energy tariff powers; similar to UPSC questions on National Solar Mission institutional roles.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about El Niño, a phenomenon cited as a factor behind rising essential commodity prices in Andhra Pradesh. How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: El Niño refers to the periodic warming of sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean.
El Niño years are typically associated with above-normal rainfall during the Indian southwest monsoon.
El Niño is one phase of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), the other principal phase being La Niña.
The India Meteorological Department factors in El Niño/La Niña conditions while forecasting the southwest monsoon.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — this is the standard definition of El Niño. Statement 2 is wrong: El Niño years are typically associated with below-normal or deficient monsoon rainfall in India, which is precisely why it is linked to price pressure on crops like rice and onions in the article. Statement 3 is correct — ENSO oscillates between El Niño (warm) and La Niña (cool) phases around a neutral state. Statement 4 is correct — IMD uses ENSO indices as a standard input for monsoon forecasting.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu directs steps to prevent rise in prices of essential commodities in Andhra Pradesh
questions.pyqLink: Tests static geography concept of ENSO and its link to Indian monsoon variability, a recurring Prelims theme (ocean-atmosphere interaction).

questions.stem: With reference to India's trade agreements, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: A Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement (CECA) typically covers trade in goods, services and investment, going beyond the scope of a standard Free Trade Agreement (FTA).
The India-Australia Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement (ECTA) already grants India comprehensive, full-scope duty-free access on 100% of tariff lines.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — a CECA/CEPA is broader in scope than a plain FTA, extending beyond goods into services and investment. Statement 2 is wrong: the article explicitly notes that while ECTA gives India duty-free access on 100% of tariff lines, it remains an interim or limited-scope agreement, and both countries are working to upgrade it into a full CECA — it is not yet comprehensive.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: What are the deal contours of India-New Zealand FTA?
questions.pyqLink: Tests static distinction between FTA, CECA/CEPA and interim trade pacts, a recurring institutional-detail theme in Prelims economy questions.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding minilateral groupings and connectivity initiatives involving India mentioned in the context of recent India-U.S.-UAE talks. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: I2U2 is a grouping comprising India, Israel, the United States and the United Arab Emirates, formed to cooperate on water, energy, transportation, space and food security.
The India-Middle East Economic Corridor (IMEC) was announced in 2023 on the sidelines of a G20 Summit held in India.
IMEC envisages connectivity between India and Europe via the Middle East without any Gulf country serving as a transit point.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — I2U2 (India, Israel, UAE, US) was formed in 2021, as the article notes. Statement 2 is correct — IMEC was announced in 2023 at the G20 Summit in New Delhi. Statement 3 is wrong: IMEC's entire premise is connectivity through the Gulf, with UAE and Saudi Arabia as key transit links before reaching Europe via Israel/Jordan — removing Gulf transit would defeat its purpose.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: Rubio pushes for India to buy more U.S., Venezuelan oil
questions.pyqLink: Tests static knowledge of minilateral groupings (I2U2) and connectivity corridors (IMEC), a frequently tested IR current-affairs-to-static theme.

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of institutions and their roles, in the context of recent economic and cyber-security developments. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
pairs: Reserve Bank of India Monetary Policy Committee
Decides the policy repo rate through majority vote of its members
Securities and Exchange Board of India
Statutory regulator for the securities market that proposed the SME IPO reforms
CERT-In (Indian Computer Emergency Response Team)
Nodal cyber security agency functioning under the Ministry of Home Affairs
Defence Cyber Agency
Tri-services agency under the Ministry of Defence handling cyber warfare for the armed forces
questions.explanation: Pair 1 is correct — the RBI MPC's six members voted 4-2 on the rate hike, as reported. Pair 2 is correct — SEBI, the statutory securities regulator, proposed the SME IPO reforms. Pair 3 is wrong: CERT-In functions under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), not the Ministry of Home Affairs — a classic near-miss ministry substitution. Pair 4 is correct — the Defence Cyber Agency, which alerted SBI, is the tri-services cyber command under the Ministry of Defence.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Data breach: SBI admits exposure of its customer data on the Dark Web
questions.pyqLink: Tests static institutional detail — statutory vs executive bodies and their parent ministries — a staple 'correctly matched pairs' theme in recent Prelims papers.

questions.stem: With reference to cyber security governance in India, which one of the following best describes the role of CERT-In (Indian Computer Emergency Response Team)?
options: It is the statutory market regulator responsible for mandating listed companies to disclose material cyber incidents under securities law.

It is the national nodal agency, functioning under the Information Technology Act, 2000, for collecting, analysing and disseminating information on cyber incidents and coordinating emergency response.
It is a tri-services agency under the Ministry of Defence responsible for conducting offensive and defensive cyber operations for the armed forces.
It is an autonomous industry body that certifies private cyber security firms empanelled to conduct private-sector cyber audits.
questions.explanation: CERT-In was established under Section 70B of the Information Technology Act, 2000, and serves as India's national nodal agency for cyber incident response, as reflected in the article where CERT-In alerted SBI and an empanelled agency investigated the breach. Option A describes SEBI's disclosure mandate, not CERT-In. Option C describes the Defence Cyber Agency. Option D wrongly frames CERT-In, a government agency, as a mere private-industry certifying body.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Data breach: SBI admits exposure of its customer data on the Dark Web
questions.pyqLink: Tests static syllabus concept of statutory cyber security institutions under the IT Act, 2000, akin to past questions on CERT-In's statutory basis.

questions.stem: Consider the following two statements in the context of the Vidyarambham ceremony observed in Keralam on Vijayadashami.
statements: Statement-I: Vidyarambham, the ceremonial initiation of a child into learning observed in Kerala, is traditionally conducted on Vijayadashami.

Statement-II: Vijayadashami, besides marking the victory of Rama over Ravana, is associated in many regions with the worship of Goddess Saraswati, the deity of learning, making it an auspicious day to begin a child's education.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I is correct — the article describes thousands of children undergoing Vidyarambham/Harishree initiation at Kerala temples on Vijayadashami. Statement-II is correct and is the correct explanation: Vijayadashami falls at the culmination of Navratri, during which Saraswati puja (learning/knowledge worship) is observed in many regions, which is precisely why it is considered the most auspicious day to begin a child's formal learning.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: Golden letters, little fingers and a leap into the world of learning: thousands of children enter world of knowledge on Vijayadashami in Keralam
questions.pyqLink: Tests static syllabus understanding of regional festival traditions and their religious-cultural rationale, similar to past questions linking festivals to their underlying significance.

questions.stem: With reference to the Enforcement Directorate (ED), the agency examining the CMRL-Exalogic payoff case, consider the following statements: 1. The Enforcement Directorate functions under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance. 2. The Enforcement Directorate can register a case (an Enforcement Case Information Report) under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 only after a predicate/scheduled offence has been registered by another law enforcement agency. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Enforcement Directorate functions under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance.
The Enforcement Directorate can register a case under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 only after a predicate/scheduled offence has been registered by another law enforcement agency.
questions.explanation: The ED is a statutory law enforcement agency under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, administering the PMLA 2002, FEMA 1999 and FEOA 2018. As affirmed by courts, money laundering is dependent on a 'scheduled offence'; the ED can proceed under PMLA only once a predicate offence (FIR/complaint) exists with another investigating agency such as the police or CBI. Both statements are therefore correct.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: CMRL-Exalogic payoff case: RMP, associate of ruling UDF in Keralam, opposes govt. stand in HC
questions.pyqLink: Tests institutional mandate of ED and the predicate-offence doctrine under PMLA; similar to UPSC 2022 question on statutory bodies under the Ministry of Finance

questions.stem: The Forest department's elephant-crossing project on NH 85 in Idukki is being funded through the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI). In this context, consider the following statements: 1. The National Highways Authority of India is an autonomous body functioning under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. 2. The Central Road and Infrastructure Fund, from which highway projects can be financed, is funded through a cess levied on petrol and high-speed diesel. 3. Funds for National Highway projects can be sourced only through budgetary support from the Consolidated Fund of India and not through market borrowings. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The National Highways Authority of India is an autonomous body functioning under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
The Central Road and Infrastructure Fund is funded through a cess levied on petrol and high-speed diesel.
Funds for National Highway projects can be sourced only through budgetary support from the Consolidated Fund of India and not through market borrowings.
questions.explanation: NHAI, set up under the NHAI Act 1988, is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, and the Central Road and Infrastructure Fund (renamed from the Central Road Fund) is financed through a cess on petrol and diesel. Statement 3 is wrong because NHAI also raises resources through market instruments such as NHAI bonds, InvITs and the Toll-Operate-Transfer model, not budgetary support alone.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Forest dept. all set to build elephant crossings on Gap Road in Idukki
questions.pyqLink: Tests infrastructure financing mechanisms (cess-funded roads, NHAI borrowing instruments); similar in spirit to UPSC questions on National Investment and Infrastructure Fund/InvITs

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding elephant conservation in India, in the context of the Forest department's plan to build elephant underpasses in Idukki: 1. The Asian elephant is listed in Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, which accords it the highest level of legal protection. 2. Project Elephant is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched in 1992 to provide financial and technical support to major elephant range States. 3. Elephant corridors in India are declared exclusively through statutory notification under the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980. 4. India holds more than half of the world's wild Asian elephant population. How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: The Asian elephant is listed in Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, according it the highest level of protection.
Project Elephant is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched in 1992 to support major elephant range States.
Elephant corridors in India are declared exclusively through statutory notification under the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980.
India holds more than half of the world's wild Asian elephant population.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are factually correct: the Asian elephant is a Schedule I species, Project Elephant (1992) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme of the MoEFCC, and India hosts roughly 60% of the world's wild Asian elephants. Statement 3 is incorrect because elephant corridors are identified through expert reports and secured by varied means (land purchase, State notifications, easements), not exclusively through Forest (Conservation) Act notification.

questions.sourceTitle: Forest dept. all set to build elephant crossings on Gap Road in Idukki
questions.pyqLink: Tests Schedule classification under Wildlife (Protection) Act and Project Elephant; similar to UPSC 2020 question on Schedules of the Wildlife (Protection) Act

questions.stem: The leak of private cryptographic keys belonging to eMudhra, used to issue web security (SSL/TLS) certificates to government websites, has drawn attention to India's digital certification framework. With reference to this, which one of the following best describes the role of the 'Controller of Certifying Authorities' (CCA) under Indian law?
options: It is a statutory authority established under the Information Technology Act, 2000 that licenses and regulates Certifying Authorities issuing Digital Signature Certificates.
It is a technical wing of CERT-In responsible for issuing emergency patches to compromised root certificates.
It is an authority constituted under the Reserve Bank of India to regulate security tokens used in digital payments.
It is a body functioning under the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India to certify telecom network security equipment.
questions.explanation: The Controller of Certifying Authorities (CCA) is established under Section 17 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 and heads India's Public Key Infrastructure, licensing and regulating Certifying Authorities (such as eMudhra) that issue Digital Signature Certificates. It is distinct from CERT-In (the national cyber incident response agency), the RBI (which regulates payment systems) and TRAI (which regulates telecom), making the other options near-miss distractors.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Eight web security keys of eMudhra firm used by Govt. and PSUs leaked
questions.pyqLink: Tests statutory basis of India's PKI/Digital Signature regime under the IT Act, 2000, a recurring static theme behind cyber-security news items

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs with reference to the Mysuru Dasara, during which the Jamboo Savari procession was recently held: Pair 1 — Jamboo Savari : Marks the culmination of Navaratri on the day of Vijayadashami. Pair 2 — Mysuru Dasara tradition : Traces its origins to the Vijayanagara Empire, continued by the Wadiyar dynasty after the capital shifted to Mysuru. Pair 3 — Chamundeshwari Temple : Located atop Chamundi Hills, associated with the presiding deity of the Mysuru royal family. Pair 4 — Mysuru Dasara : Inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
pairs: Jamboo Savari
Marks the culmination of Navaratri on the day of Vijayadashami
Mysuru Dasara tradition
Traces its origins to the Vijayanagara Empire, continued by the Wadiyar dynasty after the capital shifted to Mysuru
Chamundeshwari Temple
Located atop Chamundi Hills, associated with the presiding deity of the Mysuru royal family
Mysuru Dasara
Inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity
questions.explanation: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correctly matched: Jamboo Savari culminates the nine-day Navaratri on Vijayadashami, the Dasara tradition descends from the Vijayanagara Empire and was continued by the Wadiyars after they made Mysuru their capital in 1610, and Chamundeshwari Temple atop Chamundi Hills is linked to the Wadiyars' tutelary deity. Pair 4 is incorrect, as Mysuru Dasara has not been inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list; it is a State-declared 'Nadahabba' (state festival) of Karnataka.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: Keralam, Telangana Chief Ministers attend Jamboo Savari in Mysuru; Shivakumar stresses harmony among States
questions.pyqLink: Tests historical continuity of Vijayanagara-era festivals into successor kingdoms; similar to UPSC questions on cultural practices inherited from the Vijayanagara Empire

questions.stem: With reference to the Cauvery river, mentioned in the context of water-sharing harmony among southern States, consider the following statements: 1. The Cauvery originates in the Western Ghats of Karnataka and, after flowing through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, drains into the Arabian Sea. 2. The Kabini river, which joins the Cauvery in Karnataka, is considered its largest tributary by discharge volume. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Cauvery originates in the Western Ghats of Karnataka and drains into the Arabian Sea after flowing through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
The Kabini river, which joins the Cauvery in Karnataka, is considered its largest tributary by discharge volume.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Cauvery, originating at Talakaveri in Kodagu district, Karnataka, flows through Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Puducherry and drains into the Bay of Bengal, not the Arabian Sea. Statement 2 is correct — the Kabini, which joins the Cauvery in Karnataka, is its largest tributary by discharge volume among its many tributaries such as Hemavati, Bhavani and Amaravati.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Keralam, Telangana Chief Ministers attend Jamboo Savari in Mysuru; Shivakumar stresses harmony among States
questions.pyqLink: Tests basic peninsular river geography (origin, basin states, mouth, tributaries) of the Cauvery, a recurring UPSC theme given interstate water disputes
